related_questions.question: What are the child support rules in Pennsylvania?

text_blocks.snippet: In Pennsylvania, child support is primarily determined by guidelines based on the combined net income of both parents and the number of children. The parent who does not have primary physical custody typically pays support to the other parent. The obligation generally ends when the child turns 18 or graduates from high school, whichever is later, but can extend for certain conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: primarily determined by guidelines based on the combined net income of both parents and the number of children

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Pennsylvania child support rules:

list.title: Income Shares Model:
list.snippet: The state uses an "income shares" model, where the support obligation is a percentage of the combined parental income.

list.title: Custody Arrangement:
list.snippet: While 50/50 custody doesn't automatically eliminate support, it is a factor in determining the amount.

list.title: Reasonable Needs:
list.snippet: Support covers the child's reasonable needs, including food, shelter, clothing, and other expenses.

list.title: Medical Support:
list.snippet: Child support includes provisions for medical support, which can encompass payment for uncovered medical bills and potentially child care costs, according to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (.gov).

list.title: Duration of Support:
list.snippet: Generally, support ends when the child turns 18 or graduates high school, but exceptions exist for certain situations like physical or mental disabilities.

list.title: Modifications:
list.snippet: Child support orders can be modified if there's a substantial change in circumstances, like a job loss or significant increase in income, according to www.gellerfirm.com.

list.title: Special Needs:
list.snippet: Pennsylvania's guidelines allow for flexibility in cases involving special needs or expenses beyond the standard support.

list.title: Low-Income Protection:
list.snippet: There are provisions to protect low-income parents from being pushed below the poverty line due to support obligations.

list.title: Enforcement:
list.snippet: The Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, Bureau of Child Support Enforcement, handles the administration and enforcement of child support orders.
